NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 869 4829 2840 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 869 4829 2840, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 28, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:00 pm via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20, current State and County Public Health Orders, and AB 361.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Boy Scout Troop 191 members, Andrew Song, Miller French and Diego Lafuente.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64303 THROUGH 64373 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $279,813.43; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090321 THROUGH
  090721 IN THE AMOUNT OF $605,088.25; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $884,901.68 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
 D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 14, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  COX COMMUNICATIONS PRESENTATION AND UPDATE

Dave Simpson, Cox Communications Manager, Government Affairs, and Ingo Hentschel,
Cox Communications Senior Vice President-Region Manager provided an update on Cox’s
service reliability, safety upgrades and customer service improvements since 2020.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 735 ADDING
  CHAPTER 8.40 (REGULATION OF SMOKING) TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) receive any public testimony; and 2)
  introduce Ordinance No. 735 for a first reading

Management Analyst Jessica Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public comment was received by Dominga Pardo, Craig Cadwallader, Alix Politanoff, Ryan
Paillet, Nico Martinez, Shalin Craig, Alma Sanchez and Janelle Paule, all in favor of the
proposed ordinance.

In response to one of the speakers, City Attorney Davis stated that smoking will be prohibited
on City properties, indoor and outdoor, in addition to the parks within the City.

City Attorney Davis suggested that sections 8.40.030 B and C each be separated into individual
sections with separate headings.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked the speakers who provided public comment.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA echoed COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s comments. City
Attorney Davis stated that the proposed ordinance would not cover construction sites as
written, as construction sites are private property, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
STEGURA.

City Attorney Davis stated that under the proposed ordinance residents could smoke in their
front yard, as long as they were not on the public sidewalk, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
STEGURA.

City Clerk Pettit noted that no public comments were received in opposition to the proposed
ordinance, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN also thanked those who spoke under public comment. City
Attorney Davis noted that the ordinance does not prohibit smoking on private property, indoors
or outdoors, including indoor portions of the Peninsula Shopping Center, in response to
MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
 City Attorney Davis confirmed the ordinance encompasses cannabis and electronic smoking
devices, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN inquired if owners of large private properties within the City
have been contacted regarding the proposed ordinance, and if they were informed of the
potential effects it could have on their properties and businesses. He noted that no one spoke
in opposition to this ordinance. Management Analyst Slawson noted that the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Chamber of Commerce and owners of large private properties in the City were not
contacted regarding this ordinance, but that staff would reach out to these groups before the
second reading and adoption of the ordinance.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE ON FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 735, AN ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA, ADDING CHAPTER 8.40 (REGULATION OF SMOKING) TO
  THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE, AS AMENDED.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 735 by title.

B.  ADOPTION OF FY 2021-22 PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council approve a Publicly Available
  Pay Schedule for the 2021-22 fiscal year in accordance with California Public
  Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) regulations.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE FOR THE 2021-22
  FISCAL YEAR IN ACCORDANCE WITH CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES'
  RETIREMENT SYSTEM (CALPERS) REGULATIONS.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE
  MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council enter into the attached
  Agreement with Pageantry Productions to provide parade management services for the
  Peninsula Holiday Parade of Lights on December 4, 2021.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the
proposed contract does not include the contract for lights along the parade route, or the
videography for the event.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the parade route this year would not include
the roundabout at the Promenade, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN. MAYOR
PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that this would shorten the route, and suggested a few
additions to the route to be considered. Assistant City Manager Davis reported that the

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
 Parade Subcommittee is considering several route options, and has also discussed ways to
spread out the lights and bleacher seating along the parade route to help spread the
spectators out more evenly.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE AGREEMENT WITH PAGEANTRY PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE
  PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY
  PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 4, 2021.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

Discussion ensued regarding recommendations for the parade Grand Marshall.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2486 - APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DECISION
  TO APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210244 AT 2 BRANDING IRON LANE

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2486.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material), and noted a change made to the resolution to modify the conditions within
Section 1, subsection G, subsection 2, subsection ii, to read as follows: “Following the
adoption of Resolution No. 341, the Property was developed with a trail area approximately
173.20 feet long that varies in width from approximately 12 feet to 15 feet wide and was
enclosed with three-rail fencing.”

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba and City Clerk Pettit noted that
no recordations have been found with the Los Angeles County Recorder’s office, in response
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired if it would be advisable for a copy of this resolution
to be recorded with the County Recorder’s office. City Attorney Davis stated that the City’s
records will be clear and complete on this issue after the adoption of this resolution.

City Attorney Davis reiterated the modification noted by Director Wahba.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received from William Beverly, attorney for the Appellant Nancy
McDonough.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS MODIFIED ABOVE BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION 2486, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, UPHOLDING THE
  APPEAL OF PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210244 REGARDING 2
  BRANDING IRON LANE WITH RESPECT TO THE ENFORCEMENT OF THE
  CITY’S PRIOR BRIDLE TRAIL EASEMENT CONDITION OF APPROVAL AND
  AFFIRMING THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S APPROVAL OF THE
  APPLICATION AS CONDITIONED, AS AMENDED.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
 City Clerk Pettit read Resolution 2486 by title.

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that there continues to be a decline in the number of COVID
cases, with only 4 new cases since the last City Council meeting on September 14. Beginning
October 7, proof of vaccination will be required to enter any indoor bar, brewery, winery or
nightclub in Los Angeles County, as well as any outdoor mega-events (10,000 or more). He
also reported that the recent passing of AB 361 allows for the City Council to continue to
conduct meetings virtually. Lastly, he noted that vaccination rates continue to be extremely
high in RHE, with 99.4% of those 65 and older receiving at least one dose of the vaccine, and
87.5% of those 12 years and older receiving at least one dose of the vaccine.

Assistant City Manager Davis reported that the City Celebration last week was successful and
well attended. She also reported that the Concert in the Park featuring the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Symphonic band will be held Saturday, October 23 at Ernie Howlett Park, and
Sunday, October 24 will be the annual Prepared Peninsula Expo from 10:00 am – 1:00 pm.
Lastly, she reported that the Tracy Austin Tennis Tournament has been confirmed for
November 12 – 14 and the Holiday Parade of Lights will be held Saturday, December 4 in its
normal capacity.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis reported on AB 361, noting that it is allows for the City to continue to hold
meetings remotely during the State’s emergency, which will be continued by resolution every
30 days.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that she attended the Equestrian Committee meeting
on September 27, as well as the City Celebration on September 25.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN announced that the City won the volleyball match against the Lomita
Sheriff’s Department at the annual City Celebration.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN also reported on his attendance at the Los Angeles County West
Vector & Vector Borne Disease Control District Board Meeting on September 9.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reported on the California Contract Cities Association’s
(CCCA) annual Fall Educational Summit in Indian Wells, as well as the League of California
Cities Annual Conference and Expo in Sacramento. He also reported that he will be
attending the virtual Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) meeting next
week.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reported on the recent authorization of the Pfizer booster
shot for those 65 and older, as well as first responders, teachers and healthcare workers.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 9:19 pm MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to Tuesday, October
12, 2021 at 7:00 pm for the purpose of a regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Steve Zuckerman
City Clerk  Mayor
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 28, 2021
